name: qi-invoice
title: Quick Invoice
description: Fill in an invoice, check it over, download it as a PDF. Nothing leaves your device.
audience: Freelancers, sole traders and small businesses who need to send an occasional invoice and don't want an accounting subscription, an account to log into, or their client list sitting in someone else's database.
useCases: A freelance designer finishes a project and makes the invoice on their phone — fill it in, check it, download the PDF, attach it to an email themselves
A tradesperson invoices for two days of work, subtracts the deposit already paid as a deduction, and adds the materials as an additional item, with the total calculated as they type
A consultant working across the EU switches VAT on at 21%, marks one out-of-scope line as VAT-exempt, and gets an invoice with the VAT calculated on only the lines it applies to
Someone invoicing on a train with no signal — the app is installed, works entirely offline, and produces the PDF without ever needing a connection

dataPrivacy.storage: None off-device. There is no server, no database and no account — the invoice is built in the browser and saved straight to the user's downloads.
dataPrivacy.personalisation: The sender's own details, currency, VAT setting, standard wording and next invoice number are kept in the browser's local storage, on their device only. Never transmitted, never shared between devices. One menu item clears it. The recipient's details are never kept.
dataPrivacy.transmission: Nothing typed into the app is transmitted anywhere. Once loaded it works with the network switched off entirely.
dataPrivacy.security: No accounts, so no credentials to lose. No backend, so no endpoint to attack. Input is validated for completeness only — there is no trust boundary to defend, because the browser holding the form is the browser building the PDF.
